title: CIC-IDS2017 Network Flow Feature Guide & Diagnostic Interpretations
section: CIC-IDS2017 Network Flow Feature Guide & Diagnostic Interpretations
text: # CIC-IDS2017 Network Flow Feature Guide & Diagnostic Interpretations

title: CIC-IDS2017 Network Flow Feature Guide & Diagnostic Interpretations
text:
## Overview of Network Flow Records
In the CIC-IDS2017 benchmark dataset, network traffic is represented as bidirectional flow records aggregated across connection intervals. Key features and their diagnostic significance include:

title: CIC-IDS2017 Network Flow Feature Guide & Diagnostic Interpretations
text:
### 1. Connection Duration & Rates
- Flow Duration: Total time (in microseconds) that a connection remained active.
  - Port scans typically exhibit extremely short flow durations (< 1,000 microseconds).
  - Normal web browsing and file transfers exhibit multi-second durations with varied inter-arrival times.
- Flow Packets/s: Number of packets transmitted per second of connection time.
  - Normal traffic rarely exceeds 1,000 - 5,000 packets/sec for individual flows.
  - Floods, DoS, and DDoS attacks drive packet rates above 50,000 - 500,000 packets/sec.
- Flow Bytes/s: Transfer rate in bytes per second. Discrepancies between high packet rates and low byte rates strongly signify tiny packet flooding.

title: CIC-IDS2017 Network Flow Feature Guide & Diagnostic Interpretations
text:
### 2. Directionality & Packet Length Statistics
- Total Fwd Packets & Total Backward Packets:
  - Legitimate TCP connections maintain a balanced ratio between forward requests and backward responses.
  - Asymmetric flows where Total Backward Packets = 0 while Total Fwd Packets >= 1 indicates unanswered requests (SYN floods, port scanning, or unresponsive servers).
- Fwd Packet Length Mean vs Bwd Packet Length Mean:
  - HTTP requests are usually compact (100 - 500 bytes), while HTTP responses are larger (500 - 1,500 bytes).
  - DoS Hulk and Slowloris often use minimal forward packet lengths (0 - 64 bytes) to consume connection state tables without transmitting payload.

title: CIC-IDS2017 Network Flow Feature Guide & Diagnostic Interpretations
text:
### 3. TCP Flags & Connection State
- SYN Flag Count: Number of packets with the Synchronize control flag enabled.
  - Normal flows contain 1-2 SYN packets during the initial 3-way handshake.
  - Spikes in SYN flags without subsequent ACK flags indicate SYN flood attacks or half-open TCP port scans.
- RST Flag Count: Number of Reset flags sent to forcibly terminate a socket.
  - High RST counts in short flows indicate closed ports responding to port scanning probes.
- ACK & PSH Flags: Push and Acknowledge flags. Normal interactive protocols (SSH, HTTP) frequently set PSH and ACK for immediate data processing.

title: CIC-IDS2017 Network Flow Feature Guide & Diagnostic Interpretations
text:
### 4. Inter-Arrival Time (IAT)
- Flow IAT Mean & Flow IAT Std: Average and standard deviation of time between consecutive packets in a flow.
  - Automated attacks (bots, scripts, flood tools) exhibit low IAT variance and uniform intervals.
  - Human traffic exhibits high IAT variance due to unpredictable pauses and read times.

title: MITRE ATT&CK - Network Adversary Tactics & Techniques
section: MITRE ATT&CK - Network Adversary Tactics & Techniques
text: # MITRE ATT&CK - Network Adversary Tactics & Techniques

title: MITRE ATT&CK - Network Adversary Tactics & Techniques
text:
## T1046: Network Service Scanning
Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts, including those that may be vulnerable to remote software exploitation. Methods include:
- Port Scanning: Sending TCP SYN, ACK, or FIN packets across sequential or random destination ports to detect listening sockets.
- Behavioral Network Indicators:
  - High frequency of outbound connections to varied destination ports with very low flow duration (< 1000 microseconds).
  - Unidirectional traffic: Total Forward Packets typically 1-2, Total Backward Packets equal to 0.
  - RST (Reset) or SYN flags prominently set without completing the full 3-way TCP handshake.
- Investigation & Containment:
  1. Determine the source IP initiating the scans (internal compromised host or external scanning appliance).
  2. Inspect whether any scanned ports responded with SYN-ACK (indicating open/vulnerable services).
  3. Temporarily isolate the source host or apply edge firewall drop rules for the scanning IP.

title: MITRE ATT&CK - Network Adversary Tactics & Techniques
text:
## T1498: Network Denial of Service (DoS)
Adversaries may perform Network Denial of Service (DoS) attacks to degrade or block the availability of targeted resources to legitimate users.
- Sub-techniques:
  - T1498.001 Direct Network Flood: Volumetric flooding of target network interfaces with spoofed or automated high-rate packets.
  - T1498.002 Reflection Amplification: Leveraging misconfigured third-party UDP services (e.g., DNS, NTP) to reflect oversized payloads to the victim.
- Behavioral Network Indicators:
  - Abnormal spike in Flow Packets/s (often exceeding 50,000 packets/sec).
  - Disproportionate SYN Flag Count relative to completed TCP ACK handshakes.
  - Forward packet sizes are small (often 0-64 bytes) with minimal or zero backward packet return.
- Investigation & Mitigation:
  1. Identify whether attack traffic is concentrated on specific destination ports (e.g., Port 80 HTTP, Port 443 HTTPS).
  2. Implement rate limiting and SYN cookies on boundary firewalls / reverse proxies.
  3. Deploy upstream ISP scrubbing or Cloud DDoS mitigation if link saturation occurs.

title: MITRE ATT&CK - Network Adversary Tactics & Techniques
text:
## T1110: Brute Force Authentication
Adversaries may use brute force techniques to attempt credential guessing against network management services.
- Sub-techniques:
  - T1110.001 Password Guessing: Systematic attempts against service interfaces (FTP, SSH, RDP).
- Behavioral Network Indicators:
  - Repeated connections targeting specific management ports: Port 21 (FTP-Patator), Port 22 (SSH-Patator).
  - Consistent flow durations (10,000 - 50,000 microseconds) and uniform forward/backward packet counts (e.g., 6 forward, 5 backward per attempt).
  - High frequency of connection resets following failed authentication exchanges.
- Investigation & Containment:
  1. Check authentication server logs (e.g., /var/log/auth.log or Windows Security Event ID 4625).
  2. Enforce account lockout thresholds, IP throttling, and multi-factor authentication (MFA).
  3. Restrict management port access strictly to internal management VPNs / bastion hosts.

title: MITRE ATT&CK - Network Adversary Tactics & Techniques
text:
## T1071: Application Layer Command & Control (C2)
Adversaries may communicate with compromised hosts using application layer protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, DNS) to blend in with legitimate network traffic.
- Behavioral Network Indicators:
  - Periodic beaconing patterns evidenced by consistent Flow Inter-Arrival Times (Flow IAT Mean/Std) and predictable Idle times.
  - High ratio of outbound payload bytes to inbound response bytes.

title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Incident Handling Guide for Network Security
section: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Incident Handling Guide for Network Security
text: # NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Incident Handling Guide for Network Security

title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Incident Handling Guide for Network Security
text:
## 1. Preparation Phase
Preparation establishes the operational baseline and defensive toolsets needed to quickly respond to network anomalies.
- Baseline Network Traffic: Document standard utilization patterns, peak hours, expected packet transfer rates, and authorized protocols per network subnet.
- Security Sensor Coverage: Deploy network flow collectors (NetFlow, IPFIX, CICFlowMeter) and intrusion detection sensors at key ingress/egress points.

title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Incident Handling Guide for Network Security
text:
## 2. Detection and Analysis Phase (Triage)
When an anomaly detection system flags suspicious network flows, analysts must perform systematic verification:
- Validate Anomaly Context: A high anomaly score flags statistical deviations from normal traffic; it does NOT constitute conclusive proof of an actual compromise.
- Correlate Network Signals:
  - Check source and destination IP addresses, destination port numbers, and connection duration.
  - Evaluate flow directionality: Unidirectional flows with high SYN flags indicate reconnaissance or DoS.
  - Cross-examine with host telemetry: Check authentication audit logs, process creation trees, and DNS query logs for the involved internal endpoints.
- Prioritization: Determine severity based on critical asset exposure (e.g., database tier vs. test environment) and attack scale.

title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Incident Handling Guide for Network Security
text:
## 3. Containment, Eradication, and Recovery
Containment prevents an incident from spreading before resolution.
- Short-Term Containment:
  - Apply dynamic firewall drop rules or ACLs for verified malicious external IPs.
  - Implement network segmentation or VLAN quarantine for compromised internal hosts.
  - Apply rate limiting or traffic shaping at upstream perimeter routers to mitigate volumetric flood impacts.
- Eradication:
  - Terminate unauthorized active sessions and purge malicious backdoors/scripts.
  - Close unused destination ports and terminate unencrypted legacy services (e.g., standard Telnet or cleartext FTP).
- Recovery:
  - Restore affected systems from clean, verified backups.
  - Validate baseline operation before returning host interfaces to general production networks.

title: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Incident Handling Guide for Network Security
text:
## 4. Post-Incident Activity
- Documentation: Record the incident timeline, root cause, flow metrics, containment efficacy, and total downtime.
- Model & Rule Tuning: If an alert was a false positive (e.g., authorized automated vulnerability scanner or backup job), update detection exclusion lists and retune model decision thresholds.

title: ThreatLens SOC Analyst Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
section: ThreatLens SOC Analyst Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
text: # ThreatLens SOC Analyst Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

title: ThreatLens SOC Analyst Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
text:
## Operational Mission
ThreatLens AI assists Security Operations Center (SOC) analysts by detecting statistical anomalies in network flow records and providing grounded context. Analysts must apply this SOP when responding to alerts.

title: ThreatLens SOC Analyst Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
text:
## Severity Levels & Triage SLAs
- CRITICAL (Model Score >= 0.70):
  - Action SLA: 15 minutes.
  - Characteristics: Multi-feature anomaly (extreme packet rates, SYN spikes, zero backward packets).
  - High probability of active DoS, heavy reconnaissance, or automated credential attack.
- SUSPICIOUS (Model Score 0.50 - 0.69):
  - Action SLA: 60 minutes.
  - Characteristics: Unbalanced flags, atypical ports, or elevated forward packet volume.
  - Requires correlation with host endpoint logs.
- ELEVATED (Model Score 0.30 - 0.49):
  - Action SLA: Routine monitoring / 24 hours.
  - Characteristics: Marginal statistical deviation from baseline; check for scheduled jobs or network backups.
- BENIGN (Model Score < 0.30):
  - Standard legitimate operational network traffic.

title: ThreatLens SOC Analyst Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
text:
## Step-by-Step Analyst Workflow
1. Initial Validation:
   - Note the flagged Destination Port and the Top Contributing Features displayed by ThreatLens AI.
   - If Port = 80/443 and Flow Packets/s is abnormal, suspect HTTP DoS/DDoS.
   - If Destination Port spans ephemeral ranges (1024-65535) with zero backward packets, suspect PortScan (T1046).
   - If Port = 21/22 with repeated connections, suspect Patator Brute Force (T1110).
2. Host & Identity Correlation:
   - Query SIEM / EDR for the internal host associated with the connection.
   - Check if an authorized vulnerability assessment or penetration test is currently scheduled.
3. Containment Execution:
   - If external attack: Block source IP CIDR at perimeter firewall.
   - If internal compromised host: Quarantine endpoint via EDR agent and initiate host isolation.
4. Document & Escalate:
   - Log case details in ticketing system citing ThreatLens anomaly score, contributing flow features, and recommended playbook citations.
